amendments.rule: A construct noun cannot take the article, so a pointed `בַּ` before one is preposition-only and the English *the* is supplied. Follow MACULA's morphology rather than the pointing. Where the chain's *nomen rectum* does carry an article, that morpheme takes the *the* the ASV writes for the chain even though English fronts it to the phrase's left edge and renders the rectum anarthrously — `לֻחֹת הָאֲבָנִים` → *the two tables of stone*, `כּוּר הַבַּרְזֶל` → *the furnace of iron*. Supply a *the* on a construct noun only where no article morpheme is present, or for a second English *the* in a multi-level chain, which the article's own leaves for the outer construct: `לְבַב כָּל בְּנֵי הָאָדָם` → *the hearts of all the children of men*. **Fronting is what the anarthrous rendering forces, not a preference for the phrase's left edge.** Where the ASV instead renders the rectum arthrously, writing a *the* before the construct and another before the rectum — `מִשְׁפַּחַת הַקְּהָתִי` → *the families of the Kohathites*, `בְּנֵי הַקְּהָתִי` → *the sons of the Kohathites*, `שְׂדֵה הָעִיר` → *the fields of the city*, `מִשְׁפְּחוֹת הַלֵּוִי` → *the families of the Levites* — nothing is fronted: the article takes the *the* standing before its own word and the construct takes a supplied one, exactly as an outer construct does in a multi-level chain. Count the ASV's *the*s and read which word each stands before, as rule 47 reads which word its single *the* stands before. **A rectum that is a proper name is not an exception.** An article MACULA segments off a toponym takes the ASV's *the* on the same terms as one on a common noun, and is never set aside as lexicalized in the name: `בְּנֵי הָרָמָה` → *The children of Ramah* and `אַנְשֵׁי בֵית אֵל וְהָעָי` → *The men of Beth el and Ai* give the single written *the* to the article and leave the construct noun bare. **But an article the ASV spells into its name is already rendered.** Where the rectum is transliterated with its article — `בְּנֵי הַסֹּפֶרֶת` → *the children of Hassophereth* — the article shares the name's unit under rule 30, it has taken its *the* inside that English word rather than as a separate one, and the *the* the ASV does write stands before the construct as a supplied one. Read the transliteration before counting: nothing is fronted from an article English has already spelled out. Mark the article `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all, as in `הֶעָרִים הָאֵלֶּה` → *these cities*.
amendments.why: EZR.2 is a roster chapter with ~90 construct chains and 15 article-bearing recta, and it met two cases rule 29 had not considered, both of which its counting procedure gets wrong unaided. First, an article standing on a proper name in the rectum: `בְּנֵי הָרָמָה` (2.26) and `אַנְשֵׁי בֵית אֵל וְהָעָי` (2.28) were both first aligned with the article `unrepresented` and the ASV's *the* supplied on the construct, on the reasoning that the article is lexicalized in the toponym; both verse passes corrected that, because rule 29 permits `unrepresented` only where the ASV writes no *the* for the phrase at all and it writes one. The corrected reading now matches 2.1, 2.58, 2.64 and 2.68, but nothing in the rule said so, and the escape hatch is exactly what a later reader will reach for on a name. Second, and the reason this must be an amendment rather than a convention: rule 29 as it stands counts one written *the*, sees the rectum rendered anarthrously, and fronts that *the* onto the article — which in `בְּנֵי הַסֹּפֶרֶת` → *the children of Hassophereth* (2.55) hands the article a second rendering it already has inside the transliterated name, and leaves `בְּנֵי` bare against the ASV. The two clauses are one judgment read in two directions — has English spelled the article out or not — so they belong in rule 29's text together rather than as a cross-reference. Nothing in the corpus contradicts either: the comparable corpus rows (NEH.7.63 `הַקּוֹץ` → *of hakkoz*, 1KI.1.9 `הַזֹּחֶלֶת` → *of zoheleth*, 1KI.16.34 `הָאֱלִי` → *the elite*) are all single Np tokens with no segmented article, so they neither support nor oppose, and no corpus unit fronts a *the* onto an article the ASV had already transliterated. The amendment narrows the fronting clause rather than loosening anything, and the last clause of the rule is left exactly where it stood.

conventions: Rule 29's fronting clause applies to a rectum that is a proper name exactly as to a common noun. `bene ha-ramah` -> *The children of Ramah* (2.26) and `anshe bet-el we-ha-ay` -> *The men of Beth el and Ai* (2.28) give the ASV's single written *the* to the article morpheme and leave the construct noun bare; the article is not set aside as lexicalized in the toponym. Both verse passes corrected an earlier `unrepresented` reading and recorded the competitor in the unit note, 2.28's being the stronger because its article stands on the second conjunct of a compound rectum whose first member is an anarthrous name. Where the ASV instead transliterates the article into the name - `bene has-sophereth` -> *the children of Hassophereth* (2.55) - the article is already rendered inside *Hassophereth*, shares that name's unit, and the written *the* is a supplied one on the construct. Read the transliteration before counting the ASV's *the*s.

Where an inner construct relation is realized by an English possessive, the possessive is that noun's whole rendering and the chain's *of* stays with the noun whose relation it marks, discontinuously across the fronted possessive: `bene abde shelomoh` -> *The children of Solomon's servants* (2.55, 2.58) gives *of* ... *servants* to abde and *Solomon's* alone to shelomoh. Do not hand the *of* to the word it stands before, which here is the possessive; rule 29's read-which-word-it-stands-before test governs supplied *the*s, not the chain's *of*.

report: Checked all 41 candidate lemma groups. Every multi-treatment bucket is accounted for by what the ASV writes rather than by two analyses of one construction: the article on a participle rendered *that* (2.1, attributive) vs *they that* (2.59, predicate nominal) is rule 41 taking only the pronoun the ASV supplies; the preposition lamed rendered *of*/*to*/*for*/*into*/*unto*/*had*/unrepresented tracks the ASV word by word, with 2.65's *had* on rule 43 and 2.59's unrepresented on rule 40; min rendered *of* vs *some of* likewise; kol rendered *All* (2.58) vs *whole* (2.64); the participle of shir rendered *singers* (2.41, 2.70) vs *singing men* (2.65).

Read the dump end to end for the asymmetry the lemma table cannot see - a supplied word marked `added` in one verse and folded into a licensing morpheme in another. The chapter's 7 `added` units are principled and contrast with licensed cases inside the chapter: *houses* added at 2.68 where no bayit is present, against *houses* carried by bet at 2.59; *their* added at 2.67 where hamorim is absolute, against *their* on the suffix at 2.66; and every added *and* (2.6, 2.59, 2.64 twice) stands between two elements no waw joins, audited against a verse-by-verse waw/*and* count of the whole roster.

The article-on-the-rectum family - 15 occurrences across 2.1, 2.26, 2.28, 2.42, 2.55, 2.58, 2.61, 2.64, 2.68, 2.69 - is consistent once rule 29's three sub-cases are kept apart. 2.26 and 2.28 were corrected by their verse passes to the fronting reading and are now uniform with 2.1, 2.58, 2.64 and 2.68; 2.42, 2.61 and 2.69 are the arthrous-rectum case with two written *the*s; 2.42's article on kol is the no-*the* case. 2.55 looks like the outlier and is not one: the ASV spells the article into *Hassophereth*, so the fronting condition is unmet and the written *the* is a supplied one on bene. That unit is invisible to the candidate table, which is keyed on the fused unit's head lemma, so it is recorded below as a convention and as an amendment to rule 29.

Numeral phrases: waws and English *and*s counted for every verse carrying a total. The only surpluses are 2.8 (two waws, one *and*, so the group-boundary waw is unrepresented) and 2.64 (no waw, two *and*s, both added) - both dispositions are rule 42's own two halves, and 2.64 is verbatim the rule's `arba ribbo alpayim` example. Composite numerals fuse where the ASV writes one word (2.6, 2.18, 2.39 *twelve*/*seventeen*; 2.64 *forty*, 2.69 *threescore*) and split where it writes two (2.35, 2.65, 2.67, 2.69 *N thousand*), which is rule 30's condition applied uniformly; NEH.7.66 in the corpus aligns `arba ribbo` the same way.

BSB: the three listed disagreements are all documented convention differences and none is an error. 2.8 waw - BSB attaches the waw to its numeral phrase, the ASV writes one *and* for two waws and rule 42 disposes of the surplus. 2.42 article on kol - the ASV writes *in all* and no *the* for the phrase, which is rule 29's last clause. 2.59 lamed of lehaggid - the ASV writes the bare complement *show* with no complementizer or *to*, so rule 40 leaves the preposition nothing. No edge was changed to move the aggregate.

Two defensible-but-contested readings are left as the verse passes took them, each with its competitor already in the unit note, and neither is a cross-verse split. 2.62 folds *and put* into the doublet rendering of yego'alu rather than marking it added - no other verse in the chapter has a doublet rendering of one verb, so nothing is inconsistent with it. 2.63 marks qodesh haqqodashim `noncompositional`, which is the one place the chapter's article treatment is set aside; the superlative *most* answers to the construction rather than to either noun, and rule 6 rather than rule 29 governs there.
